description: One user tool, in `./.dive/tools/` or `~/.config/dive/tools/`, called as `user__<name>`. A file in a tools directory's `builtin/` subdirectory replaces the built-in tool it names instead.

oneOf.description: Runs a command. stdout becomes the result; a non-zero exit, a timeout or unparseable JSON is a tool error. Exec tools run arbitrary code, by design. An input property with `format: blob` (or an array whose `items` have it) takes file refs, which reach the command as local paths. Files it writes go out through `files`: declare each by name, pass `{{files.<name>.path}}` in `args`, and the file comes back under the result's `files` with its `name` and a `ref`.

examples.description: Open pull requests in the current repository, newest first.
examples.name: open_prs

args.description: Arguments, as templates over `{{input.*}}` and, for declared files, `{{files.<name>.path}}` and `{{files.<name>.dir}}`.

cwd.description: Working directory for the process. Without one, the command runs in the project directory, except in a test run before the tool is saved, where a tool that isn't `read_only` runs in an empty scratch directory that's removed afterwards, with the project's path in `DIVE_PROJECT_DIR`.

description.description: Markdown saying what the value is and where to get it, links included. Shown wherever the secret is asked for, and by `dive secret list`.

value.description: The value, exactly as the plain string form takes it.

env.description: Extra environment variables. Each value is a string, or `{value, description}` to say what a secret is and where to get it. Values expand `${VAR}` from Dive's environment or, when it's unset or empty there, from the OS credential store (the project's value first, then the global one). `${VAR:-default}` falls back to the default when neither has a value; a `${VAR}` with no default is a secret the tool needs. A tool from an installed pack also gets `DIVE_PACK_DIR`, the absolute path of the pack's installed directory, so it can run scripts and binaries the pack ships. The process gets Dive's own environment plus these variables, except in [serve mode](/reference/configuration#serve-mode), where it gets only `PATH` and `TMPDIR` from Dive's environment, these variables, and the `DIVE_` variables Dive sets.

name.description: The file name with its extension, such as `report.pdf`, or a pattern with `*` or `?`, such as `page-*.png`, for several files.

optional.description: When true, a missing file, or a pattern with no match, isn't an error.

files.description: Files the command writes, by name. Each call gets an empty directory; pass `{{files.<name>.path}}`, or `{{files.<name>.dir}}` for a pattern, in `args`. After a successful run each file is listed under the result's `files` with its `name`, and a pattern's files come back as a list. A declared file the command didn't write is a tool error unless it's `optional`.

output.description: `json` parses stdout as JSON; `text` returns it as `{text}`.

timeout_secs.description: Seconds before the process is killed.

oneOf.title: exec

oneOf.description: Makes one HTTP request per call and returns the response body. Every request carries `Idempotency-Key` (the same on every retry of the call), `Dive-Run-Id`, `Dive-Call-Path` and `User-Agent: dive/<version>`, plus `traceparent` when the run has a trace. When the run has a run token and the URL's origin is listed in [`[http].token_origins`](/reference/configuration#param-http), the token goes as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; it never goes anywhere else, and never into the run's entries or logs. Redirects aren't followed: a 3xx is a tool error naming its `Location`. A 2xx body is the result. Any other answer is a tool error named for its kind, taken from the body's `error.code` or else the status: refused (422), rejected input (400), the run token refused (401, 403), an internal error (500, never retried; a `ref` in the body is quoted), unavailable (429, 502, 503) or timed out (408, 504). Unavailable, timed out, a network error and no answer within `timeout_secs` are retried per `retry`. The message quotes the body's `error.message`, or the start of the body.

examples.description: Creates an issue in the tenant's tracker and returns its id and URL.
examples.name: create_issue

body.description: `POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH` send the whole input as JSON. A body template, a JSON tree whose leaf strings are templates over `{{input.*}}` like a `reshape` tool's `shape`, sends that object instead. `GET` and `DELETE` send no body.

headers.description: Extra headers. Values expand `${VAR}` like exec `env`, so a static credential can come from a secret, but can't use `{{input.*}}`. A tool can't set `Authorization` on a call that also carries the run token; send its credential in another header.

max_response_bytes.description: The largest body read; a larger one is a tool error.

output.description: `json` parses the body as JSON, with an empty body as `{}`; `text` returns it as `{text}`.

query.description: Query parameters, each value a template over `{{input.*}}`. A value that is a single template whose input is missing is left out.

retry.description: Retries for a network error, no answer within `timeout_secs`, or an answer that says the app is unavailable or timed out (429, 502, 503, 408, 504, or `error.code` `unavailable` or `timeout`). An internal error (500) is never retried. Without it, a call is tried once.

attempts.description: Total attempts, the first included. Retries wait 1, 2, then 4 seconds, or what `Retry-After` says.

timeout_secs.description: Seconds before one attempt times out.

url.description: The URL, as a template over `{{input.*}}`; each value spliced in is percent-encoded. `${VAR}` resolves the same way as an exec tool's `env`, so a base URL can be `${APP_URL}` and a secret can sit in the URL.

description.description: What the tool does and returns. Agents and the plan drafter read it when choosing tools.

generated.description: The generator that wrote this file, such as `dive-go`. Set by the generator, never by hand. The desktop app and the drafters show a generated tool but don't edit or overwrite it; change it in the code it's generated from, then regenerate.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for the input, validated before the tool runs. Templates reference it as `{{input.<field>}}`.

kind.description: What the tool runs. Each kind takes its own fields, listed below.

name.description: Letters, digits, `_` and `-`. The tool is called as `user__<name>`.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema for the output. A `prompt` tool enforces it as structured output; for every kind it tells drafters what the tool returns.

read_only.description: Marks the tool as free of side effects. `reshape` and `decision` tools are read-only by default, and so is an `http` tool whose method is `GET`.

version.description: The file version the document is written in. Omitted means 1; `dive tool migrate` brings a file to the current version.
